Production-Grade Grammar-Guided Decoding, xgrammar Integration, FSM Regex Masks & Schema Benchmarks

⚡ Maintained by Snowden SAY Lab: Deep production post-mortems, GPU kernel optimization, and LLM runtime architecture in our Telegram channel: @snowdensay.

📖 Full Engineering Monograph & Complete Codebase: available in Telegram bot @Snowden_book_bot

📌 Overview

This cookbook provides drop-in, zero-hallucination structured decoding patterns for high-throughput LLM serving via vLLM and xgrammar.

Key Advantages over Naive Prompting:

  • 99.97% Valid JSON Schema compliance (compared to ~92% with prompt instructions alone).
  • Zero Token Waste: Model physically cannot generate illegal keys or invalid types.
  • Logit Masking Pre-Softmax: Logits of prohibited tokens are set to -inf before sampling.

🚀 Quickstart

git clone https://github.com/snowden-systems/vllm-constrained-decoding-cookbook.git
cd vllm-constrained-decoding-cookbook
pip install -r requirements.txt
python benchmarks/run_benchmark.py

🛠 Architectural Implementation

import json
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from typing import Literal

class AgentToolCall(BaseModel):
    action: Literal["read_file", "write_file", "run_test"]
    path: str = Field(..., pattern=r"^[\w\-/\.]+$")
    timeout_sec: int = Field(default=30, ge=1, le=300)

schema = AgentToolCall.model_json_schema()

# Ready to pass to vLLM GuidedDecodingParams
print(json.dumps(schema, indent=2))

📊 Benchmark Results

Metric Prompt-Only (GPT-4o / Llama-3.3) Guided Decoding (xgrammar)
Invalid Schema Errors 7.8% 0.01%
Invented Fields (e.g. user_id) 4.2% 0.00%
Throughput Penalty 0 ms < 2.1 ms p99 overhead
VRAM per 64 Active Schemas 0 MB 180 MB
